labels.notes: Row stays partial, unmarked (no **`btz...`** mark in any of the five files, none at HEAD either). Statements unchanged: the git diff of RegComplete.lean, SpearFamily.lean and RegCompleteCauchy.lean against HEAD touches only imports, docstrings and the body of regM_isCauchyComplete_of_complete (sorry -> E0SpearFamily.regM_isCauchyComplete_of_lf hGH hS hmax); its signature (GH -> IsE0C1CompleteCauchy M S -> IsE0CauchyMaximal M -> Causal.Flat.IsCauchyComplete 2 (e0RegMFlat M)) is the same as before, and so are prop_reg_complete and prop_reg_complete'. /tmp/rcl/RegComplete.orig.lean is identical to HEAD. The three moved declarations (IsE0C1CompleteCauchy, E0C1CauchyComplete, IsE0C1CompleteCauchy.isE0CauchyComplete) are character-for-character the HEAD text, with the same namespace GX.E0RegComplete, the same `open` lines and the same `variable` block, so their full names and types are unchanged. No hypothesis is added to the paper's statement: the summable-radii hypothesis `hsum` appears only on internal lemmas, and regM_isCauchyComplete_of_lf discharges it itself via LFSurgeryData.exists_summable (proved, standard axioms). The readings (E0 scope, IsE0C1CompleteCauchy OQ-142, IsCauchyComplete 2 DEC-31/35) are unchanged and disclosed. The one remaining sorry, LFSurgeryData.exists_isCompact_of_cauchySeq (RegCompleteLength.lean:1253), is tagged `sorry -- SORRY(btzprop:reg_complete): <obstruction>` as CAMPAIGN.md requires. It is plausibly true, not a false statement. Its hypotheses are GH, the full IsE0C1CompleteCauchy (including complete and continuous), an LFSurgeryData (countable, disjoint, closed, locally finite spears in bijection with S ∩ S0 M, so Σ* ⊆ Reg M) and summable radii. Given tendsto_of_cauchySeq_of_isCompact, it is equivalent to completeness of Σ* for those radii. The sketched path-surgery argument is sound in outline: on r = R the printed metric −2dτdr + dr² + r²dθ² (BTZ_1.tex l.268) restricts to R²dθ², so the shorter rim arc has length ≤ πR; with Σ R_i < ∞ the modified S-path has finite S-length; and local finiteness rules out a limit inside a spear interior in case (b). It leaves some details unstated (how first-entry/last-exit pieces nest when spears interleave, and why convergence of Γ along late rim times gives convergence of u), but none of these suggests the statement is false.

checks.findings_of_report: Faithful. The claim that it is « not as is » holds: B21's proof of prop:abs_max relies on finitely many BTZ lines from Cauchy-compactness (BTZ_1.tex l.1091) and states Σ*'s completeness without proof (l.1093), while prop:reg_complete's proof (l.1571, l.1574) cites it « as is » for a Cauchy-complete M, which may carry countably many spears. The rim-arc bound ≤ πR follows from the printed metric at l.268. The summable-radii remark is hedged (« may not suffice ») and is not stated as a refutation, so it is a gap, not a false error claim.
checks.docstring_contract: Each of the five files has a module docstring with a statement quote, a hypothesis checklist (CompleteCauchy, RegComplete and RegCompleteLength; SpearFamily and RegCompleteCauchy as at HEAD), a SCOPE section and provenance. Each SCOPE now names the single remaining sorry and where it lives, and the statements in them are true.
